tb_keypoints_uv_to_points — 2D typed op

• Data kinds: keypoints → points

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "tb_keypoints_uv_to_points", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

*Knob a does not change the output (measured: identical at 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9).*

*Knob b does not change the output (measured: identical at 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9).*

Usage

Image coordinates (N,2) = (u, v) -> point cloud (N,3) = (z, y, x). An exit of keypoints.

The axis convention is written in the op name because in this repo match3d.project_points, which produces keypoints, returns (u, v) = (column, row), while fuse3d.to_points(voxel), which produces points, returns (z, y, x) —— naively connecting them as "the first 2 columns" swaps rows and columns with neither an exception nor a NaN. Here they are swapped explicitly as y = v, x = u before being passed on.

A round trip with points_zyx_to_keypoints_uv is bit-identical (in the direction where z is passed).

Args:

keypoints: (N, 2) of (u, v).

z: z of the plane to place them on (a scalar or an (N,) array).

Returns:

(N, 3) float64 of (z, y, x).

Raises:

ValueError: invalid shape / non-finite / length mismatch of z.

The reprconv op keypoints_uv_to_points bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). This op has no tunable parameters; neither a nor b is used.
